content.value_statement: Angular teams need a clear way to choose Signals, NgRx, or RxJS patterns. This skill provides decision guidance, examples, migrations, and best practices for state design.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to choose Signal services, ComponentStore, NgRx Store, and server state patterns.
Provides TypeScript examples for signal services, SignalStore, reducers, selectors, effects, and ComponentStore.
Shows optimistic update and rollback patterns for HTTP-backed state.
Outlines migration from BehaviorSubject services to Angular Signals.
Shows bridging patterns between Signals and RxJS observables.
limitations: It is documentation only and does not run commands or inspect a project automatically.
Examples use generic API endpoints and require adaptation to each application.
It does not replace Angular, NgRx, or RxJS version-specific testing.
It focuses on Angular state management, not React or backend architecture.

use_cases.title: Choose a state model
use_cases.description: Compare Signals, ComponentStore, NgRx Store, and server state patterns for a new Angular feature.

use_cases.title: Plan a feature store
use_cases.description: Design state shape, selectors, actions, and effects for a complex product or user workflow.

use_cases.title: Migrate legacy state
use_cases.description: Replace BehaviorSubject services with Signals while preserving required RxJS integration points.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Pattern
prompt_templates.prompt: Use angular-state-management to choose a state approach for a small Angular feature with local UI state, shared preferences, and one API list.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Signal Store
prompt_templates.prompt: Use angular-state-management to design a SignalStore for products with loading, filtering, and optimistic deletion. Include state shape and actions.

prompt_templates.title: Review an NgRx Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use angular-state-management to review an NgRx feature with actions, reducers, selectors, and effects. Identify missing selectors and error handling.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use angular-state-management to migrate a BehaviorSubject service to Signals while preserving RxJS consumers. Include rollout steps and risks.

output_examples.input: Choose state management for a profile settings feature used by two sibling components.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use a signal service. Keep writable state private, expose readonly signals, and add computed values for derived display state.

output_examples.input: Review a product list with server loading, filters, and delete actions.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use NgRx SignalStore or an HTTP-backed signal service. Track loading and errors, then rollback failed optimistic deletes.

output_examples.input: Migrate a BehaviorSubject user service to Signals.
output_examples.output: Plan: add a private writable signal, expose readonly state, keep observables for existing consumers, and migrate callers in phases.

best_practices: Keep state local until multiple features need shared coordination.
Use computed values for derived data instead of storing duplicate state.
Bridge Signals and RxJS deliberately with framework interop utilities.
anti_patterns: Do not globalize simple component state without a clear cross-feature need.
Do not mutate signal values directly outside controlled update methods.
Do not mix Signals and RxJS flows without defining the primary state source.

faq.question: Does this skill run code or install packages?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and implementation guidance only.

faq.question: When should I use Angular Signals?
faq.answer: Use Signals for local or shared UI state that benefits from simple reactive reads.

faq.question: When should I use NgRx Store?
faq.answer: Use NgRx Store for complex app-wide state with actions, effects, selectors, and debugging needs.

faq.question: Does it cover server state?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes HTTP-backed signal examples, loading state, errors, and optimistic updates.

faq.question: Can it help with migration work?
faq.answer: Yes. It outlines migration from BehaviorSubject services to Signals and RxJS bridges.

faq.question: Is this limited to Angular projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is specific to Angular, NgRx, RxJS, and related Angular patterns.
